gen-dafont-joystix-gf-miriam-libre: Approachable and modern, Miriam Libre keeps its lowercase tall and sturdy. Joystix up top brings the arcade swagger, bold and widely tracked, so a long block of text under it feels like a calm level after the title screen.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Mochiy Pop P One spreads its letters out with a sizable lowercase and no brush-style swell. If Joystix gets made small, its arcade punch fades, while Mochiy Pop P One holds its own at larger sizes.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-montserrat-underli: Chunky pixel attitude meets tidy lines: Joystix is bold and widely tracked, with horizontals a notch lighter than its uprights. And Montserrat Underline answers with one uniform stroke and oversized lowercase, which is what holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-mozilla-headline: Joystix is arcade-bold, with stems barely heavier than its arms. Mozilla Headline sits beneath with big-bodied lowercase and a splayed c terminal, so the loud title hands off to text that feels friendly and current.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-mozilla-text: Joystix is widely tracked and arcade-loud, with only modest hairline thinning at its curves. Make it small and that punch fades, but Mozilla Text stays sturdy.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-nata-sans: Nata Sans has a large central band and wide-mouthed curves. Joystix brings the arcade edge while the body keeps a technical-pen steadiness, and that clash of moods is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-nobile: Joystix opens things with bold, widely tracked arcade lettering and a restrained thick-thin rhythm. Nobile follows in a plain sans with a minimal gap between x-height and caps, and its open mouths soften the loudness above.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-nokora: Loud pixel energy, then a dark, thick stripe of text. Joystix is best at arcade-style headings with horizontals lighter but never threadlike, and Nokora is best at carrying a wide-open s through every line of sans.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Joystix has soft contrast in every curve, plus bold, widely tracked arcade letters. It does shouting best, while Noto Kufi Arabic, a modern sans with an open c, does the quiet explaining.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-noto-sans: Noto Sans reads plainly, its lowercase filling most of the letter height and its c wide open. And Joystix, with stroke weights that differ just enough to feel alive, adds arcade mischief above that plain sans.
